source.title: Short term use of oral corticosteroids and related harms among adults in the United States: population based cohort study
source.source_type: retrospective population-based cohort study with self-controlled case series safety analysis
source.primary_file: Short term use of oral corticosteroids and related harms among adults in the United States: population based cohort study.pdf

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary article plus web appendix treated as one source packet. Bibliography entries were not atomized. All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review pending independent human source verification.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to characterize short-term outpatient oral corticosteroid use and estimate associated acute risks of sepsis, venous thromboembolism, and fracture.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants were adults aged 18 to 64 years who were continuously enrolled from 1 January 2012 through 31 December 2014 and had continuous enrollment during 2011.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with any oral corticosteroid use during 2011 were excluded to focus the cohort on new users.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients receiving only non-oral corticosteroids or oral budesonide were excluded.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with solid organ or bone marrow transplantation or malignancy were excluded.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with cumulative oral corticosteroid exposure of 30 days or more during the study period were excluded.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with a history of the selected adverse events during 2011 were excluded.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

population.label: study cohort
exclusion_criteria: history of selected adverse event in 2011

atoms.canonical_statement: The final analytic cohort contained 1,548,945 adults.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary exposure was a filled outpatient prescription for an oral corticosteroid with short-term use defined as less than 30 days.

atoms.canonical_statement: The self-controlled case series compared event rates 5-30 days and 31-90 days after corticosteroid initiation with rates 5-180 days before initiation and excluded a four-day window around the prescription date.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: The SCCS recorded only the first event, excluded patients with an adverse event in 2011, and excluded patients hospitalized within 14 days before corticosteroid initiation.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: The SCCS adjusted for time-varying concomitant drug use; 42 common drug classes were initially coded and outcome-associated classes were retained in final models.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Fixed conditional Poisson regression, offset by the log of days at risk, was used to estimate incidence rate ratios; age, sex, and race interaction terms were used to assess effect modification.

provenance.prompt_version: Clinical Active Literature Basic ATOM+SEA Prompt 26

atoms.canonical_statement: Sensitivity analyses compared users with diagnosis-matched non-users after clinic visits, stratified SCCS analyses by respiratory or musculoskeletal conditions, excluded concomitant non-oral corticosteroid users, and expanded the exclusion window from four to seven days.
